rescore_meta.rescore_note: Form-4 LONG signal stands intact (six discretionary buyers, CEO+CFO leading, no sales). But TWO meaningful non-form4 findings degrade conviction: (1) FACTUAL CORRECTION — the original score asserted no auditor change, but EY was dismissed and KPMG appointed Feb 28 2025 (8-K Item 4.01 filed March 4, 2025). This is a mid-impairment-cycle auditor swap immediately after FY24's $1.8B goodwill impairment and material-weakness disclosure. The new auditor 'fully remediated' those weaknesses within 10 months — a pattern that warrants scrutiny rather than the original score's clean-remediation interpretation. (2) FDA device-recall density is high but proportionate to scale — 25 Ortho recalls in 2024 and 13 in 2025 are nearly all Class II VITROS slide/reagent/software issues, the kind of post-merger integration friction expected after the Ortho Combinations. 510(k) pace collapse for Quidel (10->3->1 across 2023->2025) reflects the strategic decision to discontinue SAVANNA — not a regulatory shutdown. No Class I recalls, no Warning Letters, no PMA revocations. Net: original LONG verdict survives but composite tempered from 0.82 -> 0.74 to reflect the auditor-change discovery.

This action effectively dismissed E&Y as the Company's independent registered public accounting firm, effective as of February 28, 2025.' The 10-K (filed Feb 19, 2026) Page 72 audit opinion: '/s/ Ernst & Young LLP We served as the Company's auditor from 2002 to 2025.' KPMG's opinion (Page 71): 'We have served as the Company's auditor since 2025.' EY signed the FY24 audit opinion on Feb 27, 2025 — one day BEFORE the dismissal letter. Exhibit 16.1 of the 8-K is EY's required dismissal-letter response, dated March 3, 2025. rfm_tuples.interpretation: The original score's tuple QDEL-06 contained a factual error. EY was QDEL's auditor 2002-2025 (signing the FY24 $1.8B goodwill impairment audit and the FY24 material-weakness disclosure on Feb 27, 2025), then was dismissed via competitive-RFP one day later (Feb 28, 2025). KPMG took over, and within 10 months 'fully remediated' the same material weaknesses EY had flagged. This is a known yellow-flag pattern (audit-firm change mid-impairment-cycle / immediately post-material-weakness disclosure). MITIGANTS: (a) The 8-K explicitly states 'no disagreements' with EY and EY's audit reports were unqualified; (b) competitive-RFP for auditor is a defensible governance practice for a $3.4B-debt issuer post-merger; (c) EY's tenure was 23 years (2002-2025) — long tenure invites rotation; (d) KPMG is comparable Big-4 with no apparent independence/quality gap. This finding REDUCES but does not eliminate the positive of 'clean material-weakness remediation.' The original score's tuple should have read 'auditor changed Feb 2025; new auditor remediated within 10 months' rather than 'auditor unchanged.'

rfm_tuples.M_source: openfda device enforcement endpoint (api.fda.gov/device/enforcement.json — recalling_firm filter for QuidelOrtho, Quidel Corporation, Ortho Clinical Diagnostics; faceted by year and classification)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Recall counts by recalling_firm: 'Ortho Clinical Diagnostics' = 311 lifetime recalls, with 25 in 2024 and 13 in 2025 (high but down YoY). 'Quidel Corporation' = 14 lifetime, with 3 in 2024 + 1 in 2025 + 1 in 2026 (Apr 6, 2026 — Class II 'product has potential for false positive results'). 'QuidelOrtho' = 2 recalls, both 2024-04-09 (Free T3 calibrator / T3 reagent positive-biased results, Class II). CLASS DISTRIBUTION: Ortho 311 lifetime = ZERO Class I (most severe / imminent-hazard). Quidel 14 lifetime = 1 Class I (April 2021 SARS-CoV-2 high viral load false-pos, well-known and pre-Combinations). No Class I post-Combinations across either firm. Most recent VITROS recalls 2025: VITROS LAC slides (2025-07-29), VITROS Ca slides (2025-07-09), VITROS OP reagent (2025-06-12), VITROS Performance Verifier QC drift (2025-06-10 x4 reagents), VITROS XT/4600/5600 software anomaly on diluent-pack expiration handling (2025-05-09 x3 systems), VITROS Slide GEN-mismatch labeling (2025-04-14), Bordetella pertussis 16.7% false-pos rate on lots 245251 (2025-03-24).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: VITROS platform recall density is elevated post-Combinations (25 in 2024, 13 in 2025) but all Class II — these are correctable software/reagent/labeling issues, not Class I imminent-harm. The pattern is consistent with post-merger QA integration friction (Ortho's VITROS was the larger acquired platform; QDEL is still integrating Ortho's reagent-manufacturing QA into its Quidel-side processes). MITIGANTS: (1) zero Class I recalls post-Combinations; (2) recall count is DOWN YoY (25 -> 13); (3) no Warning Letters or Form 483s detected via EDGAR; (4) recall reasons trend toward software/calibration/labeling rather than core analytical accuracy. AGGRAVANT: the VITROS platform is the SAVANNA replacement — Q1 2026 deterioration is concentrated in the same VITROS franchise that has the recall cluster. The Mar 2025 Bordetella 16.7% false-positive recall is the closest to a real efficacy issue and aligns with the broader theme of QDEL having reagent-formulation challenges post-merger. Net: a real headwind but does not invalidate the LONG thesis since it's Class II only and YoY-improving.

EY served as auditor 2002-2025 and was dismissed Feb 28, 2025; KPMG appointed same day. Disclosed via 8-K Item 4.01 (acc 0001906324-25-000037) filed March 4, 2025. The original score's QDEL-06 tuple asserted 'KPMG has been auditor since the Combinations' — factually incorrect. Mid-impairment-cycle auditor swap immediately after FY24's $1.8B impairment and material-weakness disclosure is a known yellow-flag pattern; KPMG then 'fully remediated' those same weaknesses within 10 months. MITIGANTS: 8-K explicitly states no disagreements; EY tenure was 23 years inviting natural rotation; competitive RFP is defensible governance for a $3.4B-debt issuer. Other findings: (a) FDA recall density elevated on VITROS (25 in 2024, 13 in 2025) but all Class II, no Class I, YoY-improving — post-merger QA integration friction; (b) 510(k) pace collapse on Quidel side (10->3->1 across 2023-2025) consistent with SAVANNA exit; Ortho side continued through Oct 2025 with new cardiac troponin clearance; (c) Carlyle has not mentioned QuidelOrtho in any of its own filings since the 2022 merger-close 8-K — confirms passive distribution; (d) None of Quest/LabCorp/McKesson/Cardinal Health name QDEL in their filings — the 11% customer is opaque to public-co cross-check; (e) USPTO ODP confirms engineering reallocation to Ortho/VITROS post-SAVANNA; (f) UCC-proxy ELEVATED_LIEN_EXPOSURE entirely explained by disclosed Credit Agreement; (g) Bristol County complaint isolated — no co-defendants, no related cluster.
